builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Should You Split Decode? Disaggregation Across Future Models and Accelerators
summary: The paper compares prefill/decode disaggregation against further attention/FFN disaggregation for LLM inference serving. It finds no robust deployment-level advantage for the finer split in SLO goodput per kW, while AFD adds communication overhead, placement constraints, and a third provisioned resource pool; any nominal lead typically stems from fitting an extra prefill replica rather than a more efficient decode pool. The approach fails if hardware mappings are fixed early, as advantages disappear when models, fabrics, or objectives change.
rationale: The reader has a single 24 GB GPU or third-party APIs and cannot deploy multi-accelerator disaggregated serving infrastructure, so this large-scale systems research does not apply to their production practice.
technique: Prefill/decode disaggregation with adjustable resource mapping

claims.statement: The paper compares prefill/decode disaggregation against further attention/FFN disaggregation for LLM inference serving. It finds no robust deployment-level advantage for the finer split in SLO goodput per kW, while AFD adds communication overhead, placement constraints, and a third provisioned resource pool; any nominal lead typically stems from fitting an extra prefill replica rather than a more efficient decode pool. The approach fails if hardware mappings are fixed early, as advantages disappear when models, fabrics, or objectives change.
Re-optimizing mappings and pool sizes cuts median normalized goodput loss from early hardware commitment from 36% to 9% under changing models and hardware assumptions.
